culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: You are a guest on private land; each of the 12 villages is autonomous and sets its own rules. Long pants or a skirt are favoured over shorts at ceremonies.
culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: No photographing, recording, sketching or note-taking in and around the villages, especially at ceremonies. Not all ceremonies are public: check signs or ask locally; stay out of kivas unless invited and stay on the edge of dances. Ask village community development offices which ceremonies are open.
culture-and-protocol.note: The Hopi Tribe's own site was not read in full; rules are from ITCA and hopi.org.

items.text: Hopi Code section 3.15.1(A): a person who knowingly possesses alcoholic beverages for personal use is guilty of a petty offense (first offence). In addition to any jail sentence or fine, the court shall require outpatient counselling in an alcohol rehabilitation program as a condition of probation or in lieu of a jail sentence. With one prior conviction the offence is a minor offense, still with outpatient counselling. With two or more prior convictions it is an offense, and the court shall require residential treatment in an alcoholic rehabilitation unit. A person who knowingly possesses alcoholic beverages for sale or distribution is guilty of a serious offense. Under section 3.4.1, a petty offense carries a maximum of three months in custody and/or a fine of up to US$1,250 (about A$1,776); a minor offense six months and/or US$2,500 (about A$3,551); an offense one year and/or US$5,000 (about A$7,102); and a serious offense two years and/or US$10,000 (about A$14,205).

Hopi Code section 3.15.2: a person who knowingly sells, distributes, transports or imports, or offers to sell, distribute, transport or import, alcoholic beverages, marijuana or controlled substances is guilty of an offense. For each such offence the court shall impose one year of imprisonment and a fine of US$5,000 (about A$7,102), and that sentence is not to be suspended, deferred or made subject to parole, probation or other early release, except that this mandatory sentence does not apply if the defendant is a first or second-time offender or the court finds extraordinary circumstances. Each act is a separate offence. A vehicle or other property knowingly used to facilitate the sale, distribution or transportation may be seized as a civil forfeiture. Section 3.15.3: a person who knowingly produces alcoholic beverages, cultivates marijuana or manufactures a controlled substance, or takes substantial steps toward that, is guilty of a dangerous offense (section 3.4.1: a maximum of three years in custody and/or a fine of up to US$15,000, about A$21,307). Section 3.15.4: a person who is voluntarily under the influence of, or intoxicated by, alcoholic beverages, marijuana or a controlled substance is guilty of a minor offense; with three or more prior convictions for that offence in the past three years, it is an offense. Nothing in section 3.15.4 makes it illegal to possess, use or be affected by a controlled substance when authorised for medicinal purposes by a practitioner as defined in 21 U.S.C. section 802(20), or as directed by a physician.

psychoactive-substances.notes: These are the Hopi Tribe's own Code offences, read from the official updated Hopi Code PDF (title page: enacted 28 August 2012; later amendments through 2020, including H-039-2020 on some of the 3.15 provisions). They are not a restatement of Arizona state law. Section 3.4.5 provides a civil-damages scale for a person who is subject to the civil jurisdiction of the Hopi Tribe but not its criminal jurisdiction and who engages in conduct in the Territory that constitutes a violation of the Code (up to US$1,250 for conduct constituting a petty offense, US$2,500 a minor offense, US$5,000 an offense, US$10,000 a serious offense, and US$15,000 a dangerous offense). US dollars converted at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026 (A$1 = USD 0.704).
